header.name: Politics in Digital Era
header.description:
Popular accounts like the one by a former Google CEO of the 'new digital age' tend to underestimate the role of state institutions. This course helps to address this gap by conceptualising the rise of digital technologies in relation to the theories of power, in particular, the disruptive nature of technological change for the state. In this introductory course, we begin by considering the theoretircal foundations of the state by reviewing core concepts grounded in political science. In the first part, we conceptualize the idea of the state through diverse lenses, including international relations, political economy a well as theories of knowledge/power and the way these have conceptualized technological change. Drawing on in-depth case studies of impact of the digital, we then develop the idea of 'disruptive power' as a driving force of politics in the digital era.
In the second part of the course we consider the how such 'disruptive power' is being exercised, and also resisted across various contexts. Along the way we explore the major crises in world politics, including humanitarian issues, fake news, surveillance and the impact of AI.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students get familiar with themes of power in the study of comparative politics and political theory

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Classify the key theories of the state and compare the relavance of each in understanding the challenge posed by the rise of the digital technologies

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Explain the the origins of contemporary crises in terms of 'disruptive power'

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Critique theories of the state and compare advantages and disadvantages of thinking in terms of disruptive power

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: Develop new hypotheses on the role of the state as digital era expands to cover new domains of social and political life

First response to be discussed in tutorial

lecture_topics: State and theories of political economy (money)
Methodological dicussion on studying disruptive power
Analytical activism and resistance to the state
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Conclusion along with the Afterword from "The New Digital Age"

lecture_topics: AI and the future of the state
